title: Peer Reviewing
intent: formative · Communication & Reflection (Applying) · click through the process
statement: Apply your critical thinking to someone else’s work and return feedback that is honest, specific and usable.

steps.title: Read for the writer’s intent
steps.text: Understand what the piece is trying to do before you judge how well it does it.

steps.title: Name genuine strengths
steps.text: Say what works and why — precise praise tells the writer what to keep.

steps.title: Locate the key weakness
steps.text: Find the one change that would most improve the work, not a list of small ones.

steps.title: Give actionable feed-forward
steps.text: Offer a next step the writer can act on, not just a verdict on this draft.

steps.title: Keep it constructive
steps.text: Comment on the work, not the person, and a question often beats a correction.

feedForward.text: Review a peer’s paragraph: one specific strength, one key weakness, one concrete next step. See the Marking & feedback activity for how an expert does it.
